item.title: Hugging Face AI-Agent Breach and SleeperGem RubyGems Supply Chain Attack
item.content:encoded:
World's Largest AI Model Repository Hugging Face Breached by Autonomous AI Agent — Must Read

Hugging Face said an autonomous AI agent breached parts of its production infrastructure via malicious dataset processing paths, accessing limited internal datasets and service credentials but not public models or its supply chain. The company remediated the intrusion, rotated secrets, and urged users to rotate access tokens and review account activity.

  • Hugging Face said it detected and responded to unauthorized access targeting its production infrastructure earlier last week.
  • The company said the intrusion accessed a limited set of internal datasets and several credentials used by its services, but it found no evidence of tampering with public models, datasets, Spaces, or its software supply chain.
  • Hugging Face said the attack began with a malicious dataset that abused a remote code dataset loader and a template injection in a dataset configuration to run code on a processing worker.
  • The campaign was described as being executed by an autonomous agent framework performing many thousands of actions across short-lived sandboxes with command-and-control staged on public services.
  • Hugging Face said it removed the attacker’s foothold, rebuilt compromised nodes, rotated affected credentials and tokens, added stricter cluster controls, and urged customers to rotate access tokens and review recent account activity.

SleeperGem Uses Three Malicious RubyGems Packages to Target Developer Machines — Should Read

Researchers found three malicious RubyGems packages used in a supply-chain attack called SleeperGem that targeted developer machines, avoided CI environments, and installed a persistent native backdoor. Users who installed the affected gems should treat their systems and credentials as compromised and rotate secrets.

  • Cybersecurity researchers identified a software supply chain attack called SleeperGem involving three malicious RubyGems packages: git_credential_manager, Dendreo, and fastlane-plugin-run_tests_firebase_testlab.
  • StepSecurity said each malicious release acts as a loader that fetches a second stage from an attacker-controlled Forgejo host, skips build systems, and installs a native daemon with persistence on developer machines.
  • The git_credential_manager package impersonates Microsoft Git Credential Manager, while Dendreo and fastlane-plugin-run_tests_firebase_testlab had been dormant for years before receiving malicious updates.
  • The malware checks for about 30 environment variables associated with CI services such as GitHub Actions, GitLab, CircleCI, Travis, Jenkins, and Vercel, and exits if any are found.
  • Users who installed any of the affected gems are advised to treat their machines and associated secrets as compromised, remove the dropped daemon and persistence methods, check for a setuid shell at /usr/local/sbin/ping6, and rotate all credentials.
